## Proof

**Setup.** Let $G$ be a finite group, $H \trianglelefteq G$ with $|H| = p$, wher
e $p$ is the smallest prime dividing $|G|$. Let $a \in H$, $a \neq e$. We must s
how $G = H\,C_G(a)$.

**Step 1: $H$ is cyclic, generated by $a$.** Since $|H| = p$ is prime, every non
-identity element of $H$ has order $p$ and generates $H$. Hence $H = \langle a \
rangle$.

**Step 2: The conjugation action of $G$ on $H$.** Because $H \trianglelefteq G$,
 conjugation by any $g \in G$ maps $H$ to itself and is an automorphism of $H$.
This defines a homomorphism
$$\varphi : G \longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}(H), \qquad g \mapsto (h \mapsto
 g h g^{-1}).$$

**Step 3: Identify the kernel.** An element $g$ lies in $\ker\varphi$ iff $g h g
^{-1} = h$ for every $h \in H$, i.e. iff $g$ centralizes every element of $H$. S
ince $H = \langle a \rangle$, centralizing all of $H$ is equivalent to centraliz
ing the generator $a$. Therefore
$$\ker\varphi = C_G(H) = C_G(a).$$

**Step 4: Bound the size of the image.** Since $|H| = p$ is prime, $H \cong \mat
hbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and
$$|\operatorname{Aut}(H)| = p - 1.$$
By the first isomorphism theorem,
$$|G / C_G(a)| = |\operatorname{im}\varphi| \;\big|\; |\operatorname{Aut}(H)| =
p - 1.$$
So $|G/C_G(a)|$ divides $p - 1$.

**Step 5: Use the minimality of $p$.** By Lagrange, $|G/C_G(a)| = |G|/|C_G(a)|$
also divides $|G|$. Hence
$$|G/C_G(a)| \;\big|\; \gcd(|G|,\, p-1).$$
Every prime $q$ dividing $p - 1$ satisfies $q \leq p - 1 < p$. But $p$ is the **
smallest** prime dividing $|G|$, so no prime $q < p$ divides $|G|$. Therefore no
 prime divides both $|G|$ and $p - 1$, giving
$$\gcd(|G|,\, p-1) = 1.$$

**Step 6: Conclude.** From Step 4–5,
$$|G / C_G(a)| = 1, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad C_G(a) = G.$$
Since $C_G(a) = G$ and $H \subseteq G$, we have
$$H\,C_G(a) = H\,G = G.$$

Thus $G = H\,C_G(a)$, as required. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
